title: Street View Showdown
desc: Clues from landscapes, languages & road signs — name the country

questions.q: The road signs are in both Arabic and French, the landscape is arid with date palms, and the currency is the dinar. Where are you?
questions.a: Tunisia, Algeria, or Morocco — but the dinar specifically narrows it to Tunisia or Algeria

questions.q: You see Cyrillic text, mountains in every direction, and the world's deepest lake is nearby. Where?
The cars drive on the left, the street food is roti canai, and the skyscrapers include the Petronas Towers. Where?
You're in a European capital. The trams are yellow, the river has a famous chain bridge, and the city is actually two cities joined together. Where?
questions.a: Budapest, Hungary (Buda + Pest, joined in 1873, the Chain Bridge crosses the Danube)

questions.q: The language on signs looks like Thai but isn't. The country is landlocked, Communist, and shares a border with Vietnam and China. Where?
questions.a: Laos — the Lao script is closely related to Thai but distinct

questions.q: You see penguins, British-style red phone boxes, and minefields left over from a 1982 war. Where?
The road is dead straight through flat desert. Signs are in Spanish. You pass a roadside shrine to a folk saint not recognised by the Catholic Church. Where?
questions.a: Argentina — likely Patagonia or the northwest. The folk saint is probably Gauchito Gil or Difunta Correa

questions.q: Volcanic black sand beaches, geysers, no trees, and the language has barely changed since medieval times. Where?
The buildings have Dutch colonial architecture, the food is rijsttafel, and the traffic is chaotic motorcycles. Where?
Snow-capped peaks, prayer flags, yak butter tea, and the world's highest capital city (disputed). Where?
questions.a: La Paz, Bolivia — or if you count Lhasa, Tibet. La Paz at 3,640m is the highest administrative capital
